events.event_narrative: The rain gauge at the local weather office reported 3.46 inches of rain within this 36 hour period.
NWS Meteorologist Joe Laplante recorded 1.05 inches of rain at his person rain gauge.
NWS Employee Joe Laplnate from Coconut Point reported (tipping bucket by Davis Instruments) 1.27 inches from 8:29 to 8:59 PM.

WSO Pago Pago recorded 2.58 inches between 12:50 AM and 1:50 AM, while at the same time several reports were received of flooding in low-lying areas. Also a power outage in Fagaitua was also reported during the time of this flash flooding event.
Rain observations by Meteorologist Joe Laplante at Coconut Point recorded (tipping bucket by Davis Instruments): 4.27 inches between 1 AM and 2 AM.
ASCC (tipping bucket by Davis Instruments): 2.49 inches between 1 AM and 2 AM.

EOC reported tsunami inundation in the harbor area due to volcanic eruption. Wave heights of 2.0 feet were recorded there at 6:31 PM SST. Coast erosion and inundation were observed in low-lying coastal areas. Mainly Onenoa reported large debris on roads, making it difficult for driving.
Over a 24-hour period, WSO Pago Pago recorded 4.02 inches of rain, which prompted a flash flood warning for the Islands.

Saturated grounds due to heavy rainfall were reported from across the territory, including 3.20 inches of rain at the local weather office. This event resulted in a landslide in Nuuuli two days later.
EOC reported a landslide near Agugulu enroute WSO Pago Pago. Near two inches of rain in a 24 hour period was recorded at WSO Pago Paog.

For the following dates, WSO Pago Pago broke record high temperatures or tied due to limited showers in the area: ||March 4 - Tied Record > 92 Degrees F |March 5 - Broke Record > 93 Degrees F|March 7 - Tied Record > 94 Degrees F |March 8 - Tied Record > 92 Degrees F.

For the following dates, WSO Pago Pago broke record high temperatures or tied due to limited showers in the area: ||March 12 - Tied Record > 92 Degrees F|March 15 - Broke Record > 93 Degrees F |March 17 - Broke Record > 94 Degrees F.
For the following dates, WSO Pago Pago broke record high temperatures or tied due to limited showers in the area: March 12 - Tied Record > 91 Degrees F March 23 - Tied > 91 Degrees F.
Flooding in drainages, streams, roads, properties and other low-lying areas were reported in the Tualauta District. Landslides were reported in the village of Fagaalu.
Strong rip currents swept out at sea two village boys from Amanave. Thankfully the boys had a surf board with them, which made it possible for rescue within a two-hour window.
WSO Pago Pago recorded 1.79 inches of rain in the last 24 hours. Flash flooding was reported in poor drainage areas such as Tafuna county by Cost u less.

WSO reported 4.27 inches of rain during this 48 hour period. Reports of rockslide in ofu, landslide near Agugulu road, and overflowing waterfall near main road along the village of Failolo were also received during this event.

WSO Pago Pago recorded 18 knots at the most for this duration, while ASCAT pass observed 25 knots. These winds created rough conditions for mariners that capsized a vessel east of Aunu'u Island around 4:09 AM. see article https://www.talanei.com/2022/05/23/four-on-board-capsized-alia-escape-unharmed/.
Strong surfs and dangerous rip currents swept 22-year-old Niutea Laulu of Vailoa at Leala Beach.

Sea level rose and high waves crashed onto the roads for this timeframe, mainly south and east facing shores. The high-impacted villages include: Fatu ma Futi, Aunu'u, Alega, Laulii, and Tula. These villages experienced damages to roads, road closure, and debris covering roadways. A national declaration was declared for American Samoa due to the widespread damage from this event.

Sea level rose and high waves crashed onto the roads for this timeframe, mainly south and east facing shores. A national declaration was declared for American Samoa due to the widespread damage from this event.
The national weather service recorded 5.29 inches of rain within a 24-hour period due to a stationary front. This amount of rainfall produced widespread flash flooding across Tutuila.
Heavy rainfall produced flooding in poor drainage areas such as cost u less and fagaima road.
Heavy rainfall likely caused a landslide near the village of Asili. The landslide cause multiple downed trees and debris over the main road. There were no injuries.
A landslide occurred in the early morning hours of the 09th in the village of Failolo. Both sides of the main road were covered with debris including rocks and downed trees. There were no injuries.
A landslide occurred in the early morning hours in the village of Asili. Both sides of the main road was covered with debris (including rocks and trees). There were no injuries.

On January 4th, a landslide occurred in Utulei from the region of the Governor's Mansion (Maufaoalii) onto the main road. Multiple large rocks and trees fell on a taxi cab and a aiga bus. There were no injuries, but there was damage to the vehicles from the debris.

Local Media (talanei.com) reported water from heavy rainfall flooded into a home in Leone. The American Red Cross reported that they responded to the family home. The Red Cross took in the family to provide safe shelter overnight. There were no injuries.

Local Media (talanei.com) reported water from heavy rainfall flooded into a home in Nuuuli. The American Red Cross reported that they responded to the family home. The Red Cross took in the family to provide safe shelter overnight. There were no injuries.

Local Media (talanei.com) reported water from heavy rainfall flooded into a home in Mapusaga Fou. The American Red Cross reported that they responded to the family home. The Red Cross took in the family to provide safe shelter overnight. There were no injuries.

Local Media (talanei.com) reported water from heavy rainfall flooded into 4 different homes in Pava'ia'i The American Red Cross reported that they responded to the family homes. The Red Cross took in the families to provide safe shelter overnight. There were no injuries.

After the Hawaiian Airlines flight landed at the Pago Pago International Airport from Honolulu, Hawaii, passengers remained onboard for two hours before being able to deplane. Due to heavy rainfall and lightning in the area, the captain decided to keep the passengers onboard due to safety reasons. The outbound flight was delayed through late in the afternoon on the 21st.

Lightning caused an island wide power outage around 1400 SST that impacted all businesses, homes, and government facilities. The American Samoa Power Authority (ASPA) restored power for each section of the island through the evening hours.
A Facebook post shows the Vaitele stream overflowing in the village of Laulii. Due to no radar coverage and no rain gage data in the area, no accurate rainfall depth or intensity is available.

A powerful thunderstorm wind gust caused a downed tree in the village of Auto during the early morning hours on May 26th. The tree blocked the westbound lane of the main road. Estimated wind gusts reached up to 50 knots.

Due to high gusts from thunderstorm winds, a power outage occurred for most locations on the east side of Tutuila. The estimated time of the outage was around 430 SST. Power was restored around 900 SST. Estimated wind speeds reached up to 60 knots along some areas of the eastern side of Tutuila.
A powerful thunderstorm wind gust caused a downed tree in the village of Amaua during the early morning hours of May 26th. Estimated wind gusts reached up to 50 knots.

Emergency management reported a landslide during the early morning hours on May 26th in the village of Amouli due to heavy rainfall. Due to no radar coverage and no rain gage data in the area, no accurate rainfall depth or intensity is available.

Emergency management reported a landslide during the early morning hours on May 26th in the village of Masausi due to heavy rainfall. Due to no radar coverage and no rain gage data in the area, no accurate rainfall depth or intensity is available.

Emergency management reported a landslide during the early morning hours on May 26th in the village of Afao due to heavy rainfall. Due to no radar coverage and no rain gage data in the area, no accurate rainfall depth or intensity is available.

Emergency management reported a landslide during the early morning hours on May 26th between the villages of Fagamutu and Atauloma due to heavy rainfall. Large rocks and dirt covered both the eastbound and westbound lanes. Due to no radar coverage and no rain gage data in the area, no accurate rainfall depth or intensity is available.

Emergency Management reported a landslide due to heavy rainfall between the villages of Fitiuta and village of Ta'u on the island of Ta'u during the early morning hours of May 17th. The landslide caused large boulders to topple over the only road that connects the two villages. Heavy rainfall also cause erosion underneath the road to create significant damage to the roadway making it impassible. There were no injuries.

Sagamea stream overflowed early Tuesday morning from heavy rainfall to cause debris flow to occur on both westbound and eastbound lanes of the main road in the village of Nu'uuli. The overflowed stream sent rocks, wood, tree limbs, and garbage to cover the roadway.

A WSO Pago Pago employee reported a landslide in the Village of Amanave. The landslide occurred in the early morning hours on July 18th. The landslide blocked the westbound lane of the main road with dirt and boulders. The road was cleared by the middle of the day. There were no injuries.

Heavy surf impacted most of south facings shores of Tutuila but most especially from Avau to Matuu and from Alao to Cape Matatula.  Surf of 20 feet forced the closure of Avau Beach on the 24th and the 25th.  Some coastal flooding were reported during high tides from Pagai to Cape Matatula.  No significant damages were reported.
Due to rough seas and high winds, a navigational shipping buoy became dislodged from Taema Bank and ran ashore into a coral reef bank along the coastline of Nu'uuli village (Coconut Point).

ASPA (American Samoa Power Authority) Executive Director, Wallon Young, said an employee decided to burn his trash on it's premises on the evening of September 17th. He said strong winds caused the fire to spread to an open 40 foot container. The fire department responded to put out the fire.
High winds along the coast of Nuuuli village (Coconut Point) caused downed power lines leading to multiple power outages in the area.

Due to the heavy rainfall on the morning of December 14th, ASPA (American Samoa Power Authority) reported shutting off water wells  to prevent further contamination of water. A boil water notice was issued. Shutting off wells caused schools to postpone.
A landslide occurred in the village of Amanave. Dirt and rocks covered the westbound lane of the main roadway.
Emergency management reported a landslide in the village of Poloa on the morning of the 16th. Nobody was injured. The exact time of the landslide is unknown.
With gusts reaching around 46 MPH (40 knots), large boxes that were decorated for Christmas fell to the ground and damaged the decorations.
Emergency Management reported a landslide in the village of Aoa on the morning of the 16th. Nobody was injured. The exact timing of the landslide is unknown.
Due to heavy rainfall, a stream overflowed to bring small rocks and other debris to cover the main roadway.
Emergency Management reported major flooding on Fagaima Road due to poor water drainage in the area.

The main road through the village of Leloaloa was covered in at least 6 inches of water and flowing into residential areas due  to flash flooding. Rainfall estimated over 2 inches in the region between 2:50 and 4:50 PM. Local Red Cross reports of one family from a residential home needed assistance.

Flash flooding caused the roadway between WSO Pago Pago and the airport covered with water and significant ponding on surrounding properties. WSO Pago Pago recorded 2.15 inches of rain between 02:50 PM and 04:50 PM.

A video from social media shows significant flooding from a stream flowing from Mt. Alava to the village of Vatia. Video shows areal flooding of properties from the overflowing stream. Rainfall is estimated around 3 inches in the area between 2:50 and 4:50 PM. The local red cross office reports there was a family in need of assistance in the region.
Significant ponding on the Fagaima road caused water to flow onto residential properties due to flash flooding. Estimated rainfall over the region is between 2:50 PM and 4:50 PM is 3 inches.

Local Red Cross office reports three homes damaged due to flooding in the Ottoville/Kokoland region. There were no injuries. An estimated 2.5 inches of rain fell between 7:05 PM and 8:50 PM in the region.

Significant flooding occurred on Fagaima road due to flash flooding and poor storm water drainage. Water flowed onto residential properties in the region. An estimated 7.5 inches of rain fell in the area on the 25th and 26th. An estimated 2.5 inches of rain fell between 6:50 AM and 8:50 AM on the 26th.

On the afternoon of January 22nd, water from surf crashed over a seawall along the shoreline in the village of Fagasa. Social media video shows at least 6 inches of water on the roadway and flooding into properties located near the shoreline.

Facebook photos show a flooded park and church along the northern coastline in the village of Faleasao. Other pictures in the area show ocean debris that moved onto residential properties caused by surf from strong/long period northerly swell, which occurred during the afternoon of January 22nd through the morning of January 23rd. Surf heights are estimated to have reached up to 18 feet.

A resident from the village of Malota shared pictures of ocean debris along the coastline of the village and flooding damage to a traditional Samoan kitchen. Strong/long period northerly swell caused high surf during the afternoon of January 22nd through the morning of January 23rd. Surf heights are estimated to have reached up to 18 feet.

A landslide occurred in the village of Amouli during the morning hours on February 21st. Rocks and dirt covered both westbound and eastbound lanes of the main road, which made it impassible. This is the only roadway to access Amouli and villages to the east of Amouli from the west side of the island. The debris was fully removed by the evening hours.

A landslide occurred in the morning hours of February 21st along the main road in the village of Auto. Rocks and dirt covered both sides of the road, but the public reported that medium sized cars could pass through. The debris was cleared later in the morning.

Emergency Management reports fallen tree branches along the main road in the villages of Laulii and Onesosopo. NWS employee reports downed banana trees in both villages. Damage caused by wind gusts estimated around 60 mph at times between 8:30 PM and 11 PM.

At 10:30 PM, American Samoa Power Authority (ASPA) posted on social media reporting multiple power outages across Tutuila due to strong winds and heavy rainfall. NWS employee reported multiple villages without power on the east side of the island. Estimated wind gusts reached around 60 mph at times between 9 PM and 10:30 PM in areas vulnerable to higher wind gusts throughout the island.

At 11:30 PM, American Samoa Telecommunications Authority (ASTCA) reports on social media of widespread outages of landline, IPTV, and broadband services from the villages of Atu?u to Onenoa. Estimated wind gusts reached up to 60 mph at times between 8:30 PM and 11:30 PM.
NWS employee reports a small hut (umu) was blown down in the village of Failolo. Debris |from the hut was scattered along the main road. Estimated wind gusts reached up to 60 |mph in the area.

NWS Employee reports a small landslide in the village of Asili. Debris did not reach the main road. Landslide likely caused by recent significant rainfall due to an estimated 3 inches of rain within 9 PM and 11 PM.
An NWS employee reports a downed breadfruit (ulu) tree in the village of Ili?ili across from iakina. Estimated wind gusts reached up to around 60 mph in the region.

A NWS employee reports multiple overflowing  streams caused widespread flooding on the |main road in the village of Nu?uuli. Debris from upstream also covered the roadway. Estimated rainfall between 9 PM and 11 PM was 3 inches in the region.

Local broadcast media reports that the Department of Search and Rescue began searching for a man who was swept out at sea due to rough seas while swimming along the coastline of Fogagogo village on the afternoon of April 2nd. Due to continuing rough sea conditions, the search operation was limited throughout the overnight hours on the 2nd and the morning of the 3rd, but resumed on the afternoon of the 3rd. The search continued through the 8th. The body was not found.
At least 6 inches of water covered the Fagaima Road between the TMO Hardware region and the Georgina Building. Water was seen flowing onto properties and flooding areas along the roadway.

Gusty winds caused downed banana trees along the roadway near O&O wholesale store. The banana trees covered the westbound lane of the main road. Estimated winds gusts are near 50 mph due to heavy rainfall from thunderstorms.
A landslide occurred along a sharp turn along the main road between the villages of Utulei and Faga'alu. Rocks and dirt moved onto the main road through the early morning hours on the 14th.
A landslide occurred in the village of Failolo on the the morning of December 4th. Rocks and dirt moved onto the main road making travel hazardous. There were no injuries.

A house in the village of Leone was flooded due to heavy rainfall. There were no injuries, but water covered the entire first floor of the house. The owner of the house called WSO Pago Pago in the early evening hours. Estimated rainfall that day through 6 PM for Leone is 2 inches.

Local police and a WSO Pago Pago employee reported flash flooding occurred along Fagaima Road on the morning of the 10th. At least 6 inches of water was flowing from the TMO intersection to the Georgina Building. Significant ponding of at least 3 feet occurred near the Georgina building. Water was seen flowing into multiple residential buildings in the area. Rainfall estimated to be around 5 inches between 8 AM and 12 PM with and estimated 8 inches of total rainfall on the 10th.

American Samoa Emergency Management office reports flash flooding occurred near the correctional facility in Tafuna on the morning of the 10th. Significant water from the Taumata and Vaitele streams overflowed the region's ditch systems onto the road at Lions Park. Pictures show around 6 inches of water moved over the roadway as the water moved into the Pala Lagoon as well as significant ponding over the area. Damage to the correctional facility and park is unknown.
An NWS employee reported an uprooted Koa tree to the east of Pago Pago Gas Station in the village of Pago Pago on the early morning hours of the 07th.

American Samoa Homeland Security in Ta���u reported a landslide in the village of Faleasao on Ta���u island. A boulder tumbled down to the main road on island. The boulder took up the majority of the eastbound and westbound lanes to make the road impassible. The landslide occurred overnight on 05th/early 06th blocking the only roadway to connect the west side and east side of the island. Three inches of rainfall is estimated during this time for Ta'u island. The debris from the landslide was cleared on late in the afternoon.

Local media and numerous facebook posts reported heavy rainfall along the villages of Laulii and Aumi on the morning of January 10th. This led to a considerable amount of rainwater to flow down Pioa mountain to move through the villages and into Laulii Bay. Residents complained of red sediment and water moving into multiple residential buildings during this time. Videos showed over 6 inches of water flowing through streets of the villages along with flooded houses.

Multiple Facebook posts show a damage rooftop to the Samoana High School building in the village of Utelei. Damage was caused by high winds along the village during the afternoon hours. Due to this damage, along with high winds and heavy rainfall, the governor ordered all public schools to close for all islands of American Samoa for the rest of the day and Friday.

Pictures from a Facebook post show the Maloata Bridge flooded due to rainfall flowing off of Lealafaalava mountain. At least 6 inches of water was seen flowing onto the bridge and overflowing into the Maloata stream.

Widespread damage to government Christmas decorations occurred throughout the island due to high winds and gusts on the afternoon of the 9th. Pictures from social media show the majority of the destroyed decorations near the Pago Pago Harbor region.

American Samoa EOC (Emergency Operations Center) reported a flooded home in the village of Alao due to the overflowing Vaimumu stream. Water covered the residential floor. An estimated 5.5 inches fell in the region between 8 AM and 12 PM.

American Samoa EOC (Emergency Operations Center) reported a flooded home in the village of Faga���alu due to heavy rainfall and the overflowing Faga'alu stream. Rainfall is estimated to be between 5 and 5.5 inches in this region between 8 AM and 12 PM.

Assistance was requested for Red Cross due to a flooded home in the village of Nuuuli on the morning of the 10th. Due to storm water drainage issues at Nuuuli (Coconut Point), flash flooding overflowed the drainage system. This water flowed onto driveway and inside home.

Members of the public, via multiple phone calls to WSO Pago Pago, reported numerous downed banana trees due to strong wind gusts on the 09th in the late morning/early afternoon hours along the main road of the villages of Matu'u and Faganeanea. A Public Works crew cleaned the westbound lane during the afternoon.

American Samoa Public Works reported a downed tree caused by strong gusty winds on the morning/early evening of the 09th in the village of Alofau. The tree covered both sides of the road. Public Works cleared the road by mid-afternoon.
Local news reported a landslide between the villages of Poloa and Amanave on the morning of the 09th. The landslide covered the westbound lane of the main road.
A WSO Pago Pago employee reports multiple banana trees downed at Coconut Point due to strong wind gusts overnight on the 07th and the morning of the 08th.

A speed limit sign and pole were uprooted from the ground on the morning of the 8th due to strong gusty winds. The speed limit sign was on the intersection of the airport road and tradewinds road on the corner of the American Samoa Emergency Management Office.

On the morning of the 8th, a WSO Pago Pago employee reported strong gusty winds uprooted banana trees along the village of Matu���u. The banana trees laid along the westbound lane throughout the morning. A local crew cleared the road later that morning.

On the morning of the 8th, heavy rainfall caused significant ponding along the airport road to enter the airport. Ponding of this region reach up to around 3 feet, which eventually drained into the airport parking lot and federal property along the airport. WSO Pago Pago recorded 2.47 inches of rain from 6 AM to 12 PM.
Local news reported a landslide in the village of Fagasa on the morning of the 9th. The extent of the property damage is unknown.

On the afternoon of the 6th, a WSO Pago Pago employee reported a tree snapped in half due to strong and gusty winds throughout the late morning and early afternoon hours along the village of Amouli. The snapped tree covered the westbound lane of the main road.

On the evening of the 4th, a road in front of the Mormon Church along the Fatuoaiga region was flooded from recent rainfall. With heavy rainfall, poor storm drainage, and large scale construction in the area, ponding of the road reached up to a foot.

On the evening of the 4th, local police reported debris on the roadway along the main road in the village of Auto. Debris flowed down Palapala mountain via Mulialeuai stream. The police sited navigation in the area for local vehicle was ���hard to pass through���. An estimated 3.5 inches of rain occurred in the region from 3:50 PM to 6:50 PM.

Multiple pictures and videos were sent to the WSO Pago Pago Facebook page showing a  funnel cloud to the south of the airport from Tutuila island around 11 AM. There was not enough evidence to show the circulation reaching the surface of the ocean to become a waterspout.
A NWS employee reported numerous banana trees downed from strong gusty winds in the harbor area near the village of Utulei.
An NWS employee reports a downed banana trees along with numerous downed coconuts and coconut fronds at Coconut Point from strong wind gusts.
A local from the village of Tula reported downed power lines from high wind gusts in the area on the afternoon of the 17th.
A NWS employee observed rapidly flowing water along Fagaima road early in the afternoon on the 17th. Water can be also be seen flowing onto residential properties.
An NWS employee reported a downed ulu tree from strong wind gusts along the Fagaima region.
A banana farmer called WSO Pago Pago to report that about half of his banana trees were downed due to strong gusty winds in the Leone area.
A Tutuila resident reported a downed coconut tree in Faga'alu village from strong gusty winds midday on the 18th. The tree covered both sides of the main road.
A resident from Alofau village reported a downed tree on a road from strong gusty winds. The tree covered most of the roadway.
A resident from Utulei village reported a roof blown off of a house from high wind gusts on the afternoon of the 18th. There were no injuries.
An NWS employee reported an uprooted tree in Amaluia village from high wind gusts on the evening of the 18th.

A Facebook video showed sheet metal ripped off a roof of the Starkist plant in Satala village in the late afternoon/early evening hours of the 18th. The flying debris did not cause injuries. Starkist shut down their plant for the rest of the day and on the 19th due to the damage and high winds.
A member of the public reported significant damage to a banyan tree in front of the Executive Office Building in Utulei village due to high wind gusts.
An NWS employee reported an uprooted tree in Gataivai village due to high wind gusts on the morning of the 19th.
An NWS employee reported a downed tree from high wind gusts covering the roadway in the Fagaima region.
A resident from Aoa village reported multiple trees downed by high wind gusts. These trees covered the main road making it unaccessible.

A member of the public reported a collapsed stone wall in Nu'uuli village that resulted in a landslide, which caused debris to cover the westbound lane of the main road. There were no injuries. Estimated rainfall was over 3 inches in the early morning through the early afternoon hours on the 19th with an already moist surface from previous rainfall from the episode.

A resident of Auto reported flooded fields and homes flooding in the village. Total estimated rainfall for the morning hours of the 19th is 4 inches. This rainfall led to a rapid increase in the Mulialevai Stream that flows from Palapala Mountain to the village that contributed to flash flooding.
An NWS employee reported a downed tree from high wind gusts in the late afternoon hours of the 19th in Utulei village. The tree was located on Tramway road.
A Facebook post showed large sheet metal wrapped around power lines in Satala village due to high wind gusts in the afternoon/early evening hours of the 19th.
A resident in Ili'ili village reported downed power lines due to drooping trees from high wind gusts.

A phone call to WSO Pago Pago reported a large tree fell on the main roadway along the American Samoa Community College in Malaeimi Village due to high wind gusts. The large tree covered the entire road.
A Fagasa village resident reported a fallen tree on the roadway between the village and the National Park Service Fagasa Pass Trailhead parking lot due to high wind gusts.

An NWS employee reported significant road flooding on Fagaima road during the afternoon of the 21st due to heavy rainfall. Estimated rainfall throughout the morning/early afternoon was 1.5 inches. Due to saturated grounds from previous rainfall and poor water drainage, this lead to significant ponding along moving water over the roadway during this time. This water was seen flowing onto residential properties.

An NWS employee reported a landslide along the main road of the Failolo and Agagulu villages on the morning of the 22nd. Debris from the landslide covered the west bound land and most of the east bound lane. Estimated rainfall from midnight through 7 AM was 1.5 inches. Areal grounds were already saturated due to previous persistent and heavy rainfall from this episode. There were no injuries.

A post from Manua'tele Community Worldwide shows a landslide that occurred on Thursday morning that occurred between the villages of Ta'u and Fitiuta. Large boulders covered the main roadway that connects the two villages to make the road impassible.

A NWS employee reports areal flooding with flooded properties and roadways due to heavy rainfall on the morning of the 17th in Alofau village. Estimated rainfall from midnight to 7 AM was around 4 inches.

An NWS employee reported major sheet metal wall damage to the Peter E. Reid Stevedoring, Inc building along the main road in the village of Fagatogo near the Pago Pago Port entrance. Flying sheet metal was caused by high wind gusts on the 19th.
A NWS employee reported downed trees caused by high wind gusts along the property of the Governor's mansion in the village of Utulei on the afternoon of the 19th.
A resident of Ofu shared a video showing sheet metal damage to fences and roofs due to high wind gusts. Sheet metal from multiple properties are seen flying across the village.

High surf along the east coast of Coconut Point (Nuuu'li village) created minor coastal erosion on the evening of May 7th. Coastal flooding was observed on the Pala Lagoon side of Coconut Point. Pictures show a flooded house along the lagoon.

A landslide occurred on the roadway connecting Aua and Afono villages, Route 006, that covered both sides of the road. A picture shows large trees, dirt and rocks from North Pioa mountain on the roadway. American Samoa Mesonet (University of Hawaii) recorded over 1.5 inches in the region from the morning of May 6th through the morning of May 7th, along with well above average rainfall the prior week. There were no injuries.
An NWS employee reported ocean debris along the main road at Utumea West village and minor coastal erosion. Estimated surf heights were 18 feet.
An NWS employee observed ocean debris along the roadway caused by high surf in Laulii village. Estimated surf heights were 18 feet.

An NWS employee reported a minor landslide from Masinaoleafiali Ridge along the main road along Asili and Amaluia villages on the morning of May 7th. Rocks covered the westbound lane of the road. Estimated rainfall from the mornings between the 6th and 7th were two inches along with above average rainfall so far in May.
A phone call from a local in the Nuuuli village reported downed banana trees blown over from strong winds.

A driver along the main road in Matu'u village reported a minor landslide in the early afternoon of the 8th. A picture shows rocks blocking the westbound lane of the roadway. Estimated rainfall was 6 inches on May 5th through May 8th.

An NWS employee reported considerable flash flooding along Fagaima Road, Route 019, in the early morning hours on the 10th. Water over 6 inches high rushed violently from west to east along the roadway. Considerable damage was reported on the road with large chunks of asphalt taken away from the road and large amounts of water puddled onto properties along the road. Estimated rainfall was 6 inches in 3 hours between 9 PM and 12 AM.
A landslide was reported along the road connecting the Masausi and Fagaitua Villages, Route 011, along Maugaoalii/Usi Ridge. Damage is unknown. There were no injuries.
An NWS employee reported an overflowing stream, Mulialevai Stream, inside the village of Auto. Pictures show water flowing onto other properties.
A video given to WSO Pago Pago showed significant flooding along airport road in the Cost-U-Less/GIAS region. Rainfall is estimated to be around 2.5 inches between 11 AM and 12 PM.

A NWS employee reported flash flooding along the correctional facility region with rapid buildup of streams overflowing the roadway. At least 6 inches of water was observed moving over the road to flow into the Pala Lagoon.

A NWS employee observed flash flooding on Fagaima road midday on the 24th as water covered the entire road and flowing towards the Georgina Building. A video sent to WSO Pago Pago shows at least 6 inches of water that covered the roadway rapidly moving eastward.

A NWS employee reported flash flooding along the main road between Alofau and Amouli. Water completely covered the main road and flowed downhill. Estimated rainfall in the region was 4.5 inches in 3 hours.

A video from an American Samoa Community College student showed significant flooding on the campus roads and sidewalks. Water can be seen entering into one of the buildings. Estimated rainfall was around 4.5 inches in 3 hours.

A NWS employee reported debris such as rocks, tree limbs, and garbage from an overflowing stream, Sagamea Stream, in Nuuuli Village near H&L Mart 2 and Minks AC covered the main road. Estimated rainfall was 4 inches in three hours.

A Facebook video shows flash flooding due to water rapidly flowing from the mountains into the village. The video shows water rushing into houses and spoke of crop damage in the region. The video is from Kiei Tamate Lei���atua���s Facebook page.
An NWS Employee showed pictures of a home in Nuuuli Village with considerable flooding due to heavy rainfall on the morning of July 26th.

Emergency Management Director confirmed a deadly landslide in Gataivai Village on the morning of the 26th. Local radio station, KHJ, reported mud and debris from the landslide broke through the walls of a home, toppling the bedroom of a 61-year-old woman who died on the scene. Emergency Management reported two children were also trapped but were rescued by local responders.

An NWS employee reported a flash flood in Seetaga village on the morning of the 26th, caused by heavy rainfall. The flooding was a result of streams from the Lealafaalava and Leileia Mountains overflowing, carrying rocks and sediment that covered properties and the main road. A village resident also reported to WSO Pago Pago that their home was flooded.

A flash flood in Nu'uuli village broke through a property wall, according to an NWS employee. The flood dropped rocks and sediment onto the main road at the intersection with Nu'uuli Road, near Paradise Pizza.
A flash flood occurred in Faganeanea village due to overflowing streams from Matafao mountain. This caused a property retaining wall to break and flood a home in the village.
A resident of Matu'u village reported to the WSO in Pago Pago that flash flooding from the Afuelo stream, which is runoff from Matafao Mountain, flooded several homes on the morning of the 26th.
An NWS employee reported a landslide caused by heavy rainfall that covered both sides of the main road in Fatu ma Futi village with rocks and sediment.
A resident of Fagatogo reported to WSO Pago Pago that their family home was flooded on the morning of the 26th due to heavy rainfall, likely aided by water flowing from nearby higher elevations.

On the morning of the 26th, a Faga'alu resident reported to WSO Pago Pago that their home was flooded. The excessive rainfall was likely compounded by runoff from Matafao Stream, which runs through the village.
An NWS Employee showed pictures of a home in Nuuuli Village with considerable flooding due to heavy rainfall on the morning of July 26th.
Harbormaster confirmed minor coastal flooding of Marina.
A Starkist employee reported water from Pago Pago Harbor entered buildings at the Starkist plant in Anua and Atu'u Villages. Damage to the facility is unknown.
A Facebook Post from Fagasa Village Worldwide shows coastal inundation with water from Fagasa Bay moving over coastal roadways along Fagasa Village. Damage from the inundation is unknown.
A Facebook video from LillyJulia-Aniva Fanene shows coastal inundation from Pago Pago Harbor onto coastal roadways in Aua village. Damage from the inundation are unknown.
Surveillance video from the American Samoa Shipyard Services Authority shows inundation onto the shipyard's property from Pago Pago Harbor. Damage from the inundation are unknown.
An NWS employee reported flooding along the Tafuna Correctional Facility near Lions Park. Water covered both sides of the road along Lions Park due to an overflowing stream.

A 20 year old man was swept out to sea by large and powerful surf on the afternoon of August 06th while sitting along the shore line between Maliu Mai and the airport in the villages of Ili'ili and Tafuna, according to Talanei.com.

On the morning of September 17th, strong gusty winds caused a breadfruit tree to fall in the village of Ili'ili. An NWS employee confirmed the tree blocked the eastbound lane of the main road. Wind gusts in the region were estimated to have reached 50��mph.

According to KHJ News, a 15-year-old boy died on the afternoon of the 12th after being swept away by high surf while swimming at the Leala Sliding Rocks shoreline on Tutuila island, near the villages of Vailoatai and Taputimu.

Flash flooding occurred along Fagaima Road around midday on October 22nd due to heavy rainfall and storm water drainage issues. NWS employee Brayden Barton provided photos showing significant water intrusion into properties and homes adjacent to the roadway. Saturated grounds from recent rainfall exacerbated runoff and contributed to the flooding.

An NWS employee reported flash flooding near American Samoa Community College, with water intruding into buildings due to heavy rainfall and inadequate storm water drainage. Grounds were saturated from recent rainfall, exacerbating runoff issues.

Flooding was reported by NWS staff along Airport Road on October 22nd. Overflow from saturated drainage banks led to water encroaching onto NWS property and adjacent areas after receiving over two inches of rain in two hours as the grounds were already saturated.

A landslide occurred along the main road in Seetaga village, blocking the westbound lane. A University of Hawaii/American Samoa Power Authority rainfall station in Aasu Village (approximately 1���2 miles northeast of the incident site) measured 0.76 inches of rain between 11 AM and Noon, aligning with the reported landslide time. Soils were already saturated from persistent above-average rainfall since October, with 2.18  inches measured at Aasu Village over the broader episode. The combination of saturated grounds and short-duration heavy rainfall likely contributed to the landslide.

An NWS employee reported a landslide in Leone Village during the morning of November 20th. Dirt and debris blocked both ends of the main roadway through the village. A nearby University of Hawaii/American Samoa Power Authority rainfall gauge located in Aasu Village, approximately one mile north of the landslide site, recorded 1.71 inches of rainfall between 3:00 AM and 10:00 AM. This short-duration heavy rainfall, combined with already saturated soils following multiple weeks of above-average rain, likely contributed to the resulting landslide.
A landslide was reported at Poloa Village on the morning of March 30, scattering debris and rocks across the main road. No injuries were reported.

On the morning of March 26, a landslide was reported on Ta���u Island with large boulders and debris blocking the main road between Fitiuta and Ta���u Village. The landslide made the road impassable in both directions until early afternoon, when local crews successfully cleared the site and restored access. No injuries were reported.

A High Surf Advisory was issued on September 5 due to a series of Low Pressure Systems north of New Zealand, in which produced moderate to strong swells. These Swells affected south facing shores of the islands of Tutuila and Aunuu. Surf heights of 10 to 14 feet with occasional higher sets were observed. No significant damages were reported.

Numerous cumulonimbus embedded within the trough were moving southeast along the trough axis on the 28th of November. The Pago Pago WSO recored 1.21 inches of precipitation in less than 30 minutes. Mayors of various villages reported overflow of streams on roads and low lying areas. Debris and pot-holes were the major damages reported by the Department of Public Works. No other damages were reported.

With a well saturated ground for the islands from the previous days, a slow moving trough poured 3.59 inches of rain over the islands on the 8th of December. The flash flood warning was issued by the Pago Pago NWS for ten hours. The flash flood from the slow moving trough over the islands produced heavy runoffs of streams and inundated low lying of the islands. The Department of the Public Works reported major drainage problems and roads reconstructions. The Department of Public Safety reported overflow of streams on roads and inundation of low lying areas during this short period of time. No other damages were reported.

Surf heights of 10 to 15 ft had impacted south facing shores of Tutuila. Low lying areas of the Eastern District had debris been washed over roads and coastal erosions which created some landslides along near shore mountain areas. The Shear Line that remained nearly stationary over the islands had facilitated with these landslides as ground became saturated.
WSO Pago recorded trades of 30 to 35 kt from the 24th to the 27th. The Department of Public Works reported a few uprooted trees around various areas. No other damages were reported.

Heavy showers had inundated low lying areas of the islands on the 10th, 14th, and the 17th of the month. Landslides and large pot-holes on the main road were the major reconstruction reported by the Department of Public Works. WSO Pago issued a Small Stream Flood Advisory prior to these event dates.

Heavy rainshowers from a cold front had inundated low lying areas of the islands. The Department of Public Safety reported runoffs of several streams around the islands that had inundated low lying areas and caused difficulties of driving. WSO Pago Pago recorded 2.92 inches of precipitation within a 2 hour period. No other damages were reported.

A 7.9 earthquake occurred about 120 miles southwest of Pago Pago and it shook the |entire Samoan and Tongan region. The earthquake occurred around 648 am |Samoan local time, and it took within 15 minutes for the tsunami waves to reach the Samoan Islands.
A surface trough near Tutuila generated widespread showers over Tutuila Aunuu and Manu'a Islands.
A spotter from Leone village on the southwest side of Tutuila Island reported a waterspout near the Leone waters.

Hurricane Evan made landfall on Upolu instead of Tutuila as suspected by the Regional Services Meteorological Center- Nadi for the South Pacific region. American Samoa was spared during this episode, hence only gale force winds and strong gusts reached Tututila during the daylight of 12/2100Z to 13/0400Z. No damages or injuries reported.

Tropical Cyclone Garry moved to the north of Tutuila and Manua between 22/0000Z and 24/2300Z. Only gale force winds made their way offshores and strong gusts reached certain area on American Samoa. No damages or injuries reported.

Tropical Cyclone Garry moved to the north of Tutuila and Manua between 22/0000Z and 24/2300Z. Only gale force winds made their way offshores and strong gusts reached certain area on American Samoa. No damages or injuries reported.

Heavy rain drenched most of Tutuila during this event. At Fagaitua High School, an ankle-high floodwater covered the walkway and grounds of the campus, and water raced into some of the classrooms on the first floor. This situation could have been prevented if the drainage outlets were filtered before and during the heavy rain. The high school students were released from the school before noon.

Heavy rainfall triggered flash flooding over American Samoa. Fast flowing water along the streams and strong runoff near the waterfalls were reported by residents. Strong gusty winds associated with this phenomenon severed a few tree branches in Tutuila. No injury or fatality reported.

Combined long-period swells and trade-wind generated seas and swells have triggered the Pacific Islands Ocean Observing System (PacIOOS) buoy to detach from its moore. A storm low near New Zealand was responsible for these hazardous south swells of 12 to 15 feet...along with strong gusty winds that have impacted the dislocation of the wave buoy. A high surf warning and small craft advisory were issued when this event occurred.

The Talanei News reported a longliner ran aground near the [Pago Pago International] airport and its crewmembers had to deploy life rafts to get to shore. About 22 crew members were on the Seahawk 68 longliner and they all survived. A high surf and small craft advisories were issued when this incident occurred.

Two traditional longboats capsized just less than 2 miles away from the mouth of Pago Pago harbor during the American Samoa Flag Day race. Seas of 6 to 9 feet have impacted the race which caused the cancellation of the longboat race. A small craft advisory was issued when this marine incident occurred. No injury or fatality reported.

Large surfs of 18 to 20 feet impacted west, south and east facing reefs of American Samoa. A combined south swell and seasonal trade-wind generated swells produced hazardous surfs and dangerous rip currents. Reports of coastal erosion and debris have damaged roads, while other parts of the Islands experienced waves wash up corals on the main road. The Talanei News reported residents observed waves crash on the road while other villages suffered from the horrendous heights of surfs pounding along the affected shores. A high surf warning and small crafts advisory were issued during this episode. No injury or fatality reported.

Large south swells combined with strong trade-wind generated seas and swells have produced hazardous surfs up to 16 feet along the east...south and west facing reefs. Reports of debris and corals swept over the main highway were relayed to the Weather Service Office by residents and motorists.

The Department of Public Safety dispatcher confirmed a drowning incident of a male fisherman in his early 30s on December 28th. The victim was swept to sea and his boy has not been recovered. Strong swells and hazardous seas have prevented the Search and Rescue team from conducting their services to find the missing man. The Advisories for small craft and high surf were issued prior to this unfortunate tragedy. A strong monsoonal trough near the east of Manu'a was responsible for strong gusty winds...hazardous surfs and swells.

Flash flooding has triggered strong runoffs and landslides across American Samoa, especially over the Eastern district of Tutuila. The Weather Service Office recorded nearly 5 inches of rainfall from the hours of 5AM to 5PM. There were no injuries or fatalities reported.

Heavy rainfall triggered strong runoff especially along the central and eastern district of Tutuila. Public parking lot and roads were flooded and landslides were reported mainly from the eastern district.
Tropical Storm force winds damaged plantations, blew roofs of a couple shacks and garages, and uprooted banyan and breadfruit trees in Tututila.

Hurricane Victor generated dangerous swells and surfs...and storm surges that have impacted the shores of American Samoa.  The storm surge damaged homes and personal properties in low-lying areas near the shores.  Also, the storm surge triggered coastal erosion mainly along the east and south facing shorelines of Tutuila. The power-line, rock-walls, family yards and a private boat ramp were damaged in the Nuuuli/Coconut-Point beach area. There was no injury or fatality reported.

Very hot and humid weather occurred across American Samoa during the second week of February. New record high temperatures ranged from the lower to upper 90s, and heat indices were in the 112 to 118-degree range all six days near the Pago Pago International Airport. There were no medical reports on the impact of the excessive heat.

Hurricane Amos passed near American Samoa during the early morning hours on the 23rd of April. The strongest wind speed and highest gusts were reported from the NOAA ESRL in Matatula, with winds peaking to near 65 MPH Gusts 74 MPH. Several residents on Tutuila self-evacuated their families to avoid storm surge and coastal inundation. There were downed plantations, fallen trees and damaged outdoor kitchens reported from the village of Fitiuta in Manu'a. The south-facing shores of all Islands were heavily impacted by strong swells and dangerous surfs, and coastal erosion was noticeable along the Nuuuli/Coconut Point which impacted the road forcing motorists to drive on only one lane. No injuries or fatalities reported.

A surface trough near the Samoan region generated numerous showers with locally heavy rainfall. This rainfall event triggered flash flooding across American Samoa, and the Weather Service Office recorded 2.37 inches. No injury or fatalities reported.

A surface trough combined with a seasonal trade-wind weather conditions have triggered numerous to frequent showers with locally heavy rainfall across American Samoa. The Weather Service Office recorded 2.04 inches of rainfall while other villages across American Samoa encountered higher rainfall amounts. There were no injuries or fatalities reported.

Locally heavy rainfalls have triggered flash flooding across American Samoa, a result of an active surface trough near the Samoan Islands. The Weather Service Office recorded 2.49 inches of rainfall. Heavy flow of water along the small streams and across the main roads were observed.

Heavy rainfall combined with strong gusty winds up to 50 mph were associated with a surface trough that was located over the Samoan Islands. This phenomenon triggered flash flooding in small streams, rapid runoff along valleys and small streams, and landslides near Matafao Elementary in Fagaalu. Strong gusty winds impacted a few banana plantation across Tutuila. The Weather Service Office received 3.27 inches of rainfall during the 24-hour period while heavier showers fell near mountainous locations. Heavy water ponding were noticeable in the Tualauta region and Eastern district. Reports of immensely heavy rain were also reported from Manu'a Islands. No injury or fatalities reported.

A very active monsoonal trough generated strong northerly winds across American Samoa. The Weather Service Office in Tafuna recorded maximum sustained winds of 31 knots with gusts up to 45 knots. Damages to large trees, plantations, power-lines, and several roofs of homes and private businesses were impacted by these strong winds. No injuries or fatalities reported.

Extremely heavy runoffs, landslides, and severe flash flooding were results of heavy rain from an active surface trough near American Samoa. The Weather Service Office in Tafuna recorded over 8 inches of rainfall during the first day of this rainy event, and over 2.40 inches of precipitation on the second day. Yet, higher amounts of rainfall drenched locations near mountains and valleys. Over a dozen homes and private properties were flooded and critically impacted across American Samoa, causing several families to self-evacuate.

Heavy rainfall with isolated thunderstorms and windy conditions triggered flash flooding across Tutuila and Manua. The Weather Service Office recorded over 2.60 inches of rainfall and maximum winds of 30 mph yet much higher near thunderstorms.

Heavy rainfall from thunderstorms soaked American Samoa. This situation triggered heavy runoff and flash flooding across the territory especially near Tualauta district and low-lying areas in the Fagaloa. The Weather Service Office recorded over 3.70 inches of rainfall.

Heavy rainfall associated with a surface trough generated flash flooding across American Samoa. The main road on Tutuila was heavily flooded especially near Satala, Pago Pago, Utulei, and Tualauta District. The Weather Service Office received 3.88 inches of rainfall.

Occasional showers with locally heavy rainfall and isolated thunderstorms drenched American Samoa as a result of an active surface trough near the Samoan Islands. Strong runoff swept gravel and rocks on the main road and eroded private lands. Heavy ponding across Tualauta district especially near poor drainage outlets impacted vehicles driving through the Airport Road near Cost-U-Less and Ottoville area. The Weather Service Office recorded 5.02 inches for this two-day episode.

Heavy showers...windy conditions and isolated thunderstorms were outcome of an active surface trough near the Samoan Islands. Locally heavier rainfall were observed over mountainous locations, hence the Weather Service Office recorded about 4.58 inches of rainfall during this episode.
Heavy runoff and flash flooding affected most villages especially low-lying areas, including Ottoville and Tafuna Road. The Weather Service Office recorded 5.39 inches of rainfall.

Strong northerly winds from a monsoon trough began the morning of Dec. 17th and continued through the afternoon of Dec 18th. These monsoon-induced winds damaged several rooftops of homes and a government infrastructure, including fallen trees on homes. There were no injuries or fatalities reported.
The SPCZ produced heavy rainfall especially over the mountainous region. The Weather Service Office in Tafuna recorded a total of 1.28 inches of rainfall.

Moisture from the SPCZ triggered heavy showers over the territory. The rain produced flash flooding of small streams and drainage outlets. The Weather Service Office recorded a total of 2.27 inches of rainfall, hence, showers were heavier over the mountainous area.

Moderate to heavy rains just days earlier leading up to January 30th triggered a mudslide near a residential area in the village of Utulei, between the hours of 7:30 AM and 8 AM. The Emergency management reported a huge banyan tree fell over the roof and patio of a two-story home. The home sustained severe damages to roofing and interior of property, but no injury or fatality was reported. ||The Weather Service Office received about 0.60 inch of rainfall from 7 AM to 10 AM, and a Small Stream Flood Advisory was issued at 7:35 AM for this event. Unfortunately, limited data in the Fagaloa area hindered the Weather Service Office from elevating the advisory.

Heavy rain and scattered thunderstorms enhanced by moisture from a surface trough triggered flash flooding in streams and low-lying area across the territory. The Weather Service Office received about 2.37 inches of rainfall but slightly higher near mountainous locations.

Tropical Cyclone Gita combined with an active monsoon trough generated destructive winds and torrential rainfall between the hours of 4 AM to 2 PM. At the peak of the tropical storm before 8 AM, the Weather Service Office and most of American Samoa lost power. The NOAA Earth System Research Laboratory (ESRL) Office in Matatula recorded 64 kt gust 85 kt, and the radiosonde data reported 59 kt around 6 AM. Tropical Cyclone Gita caused widespread damages to homes, private and personal properties, government facilities, roads, electrical poles and wires, phone lines, and plantations across American Samoa. About 965 people including children evacuated to 12 shelters on the island of Tutuila. Numerous mudslides, flash flooding in small streams and low-lying areas were results of heavy rainfall. Heavy runoff swept debris and water into homes near valleys and small streams area. Several banyan trees and most breadfruit trees were uprooted. ||A cargo shipping boat in Manu'a, Uila o le Sami, sank in Ta'u. Another similar incident occurred where an alia boat sank in Fagaitua bay but was later recovered by the owners on the following day. A storm surge up to 2 to 4 feet swept debris over the main road and beach area along the northwest through northeast shores of Tutuila, Aunuu and Manu'a. There we no fatalities reported.
Heavy showers associated with an upper level trough that had moved across Tutuila dumped 3.87 inches of rainfall in less than 12 hours.  No significant damages were reported.

Frontal passage prompted a flash flood watch that was upgraded to Flash Flood Warning. Numerous reports received from residents around the island of flooded roadways. The NWS Office recorded 1.85 on the morning of the 30th.
Landslide/Mudslide reported at Faga'alu Village due to continuous heavy rainfall. A Flash Flood Warning was in effect during the time of this report at 9:50 AM SST.

WSO Pago Pago recorded .45 within the hour that prompted a Small Stream Flood Advisory on the 17th. Another episode of .38 or rainfall was recorded within the hour on the 18th that also prompted the issuance of a Small Stream Flood Advisory. Due to the same episode.

WSO Pago Pago recorded continuous rainfall over 16 hours, totaling to 1.53. Reports of flooded roads, especially as grounds are saturated were received by the office.
WSO Pago Pago recorded a total of 3.26 of rainfall on this day, prompting a Flash Flood Warning for the territory.

PacIOOS Aunu'u wave buoy observed seas of 7 to 12 feet throughout the High Surf Advisory period. These seas were mainly wind driven waves and combined with large southerly swells. They translate to surfs of 10 to 14 feet.

Calls received of flooded roads near the airport and Cost U Less due to heavy rainfall. WSO Pago Pago recorded 1.81 of rainfall.
Lisa from the Emergency Operations Center reported flooding conditions at Cost-u-less and a minor mudslide at the governors mansion.

WSO Pago Pago recorded 2.16 inches of rain within the hour. Teachers reported flooding at Tafuna High School and outside of classrooms. Midkiff elementary reports flooding near classrooms. Fagaima resident reported flooding in the front of her home about 1 foot deep. Hard for cars to drive through.
The Weather Service office in Pago Pago recorded 4.98 inches of rain combined for the 12th and 13th of May.
The Weather Service Office Pago Pago recorded 2.20 inches of rain within in the 18 hour period.
Reports in Coconut Point, Nuuuli of coastal inundation in front yards and graves completely underwater.
Plane went into airport pond due to high winds.
USCG reported increased frequency of winds in the Pago Pago Harbor. Wise Honest Vessel anchored in the harbor was swaying back and forth due to strong winds.

Numerous callers reported flooded roadways. One caller from the village of Leone reported flooding in his home due to continuous rainfall within the 72 hours. The Weather Service office recorded 8.41 inches of rain for the duration of this period.
EOC called with 2 mudslides ; first in ASAO, the second at Alataua elementary at Nua and Seetaga. Mudslide reported damage to Alataua elementary library.
The weather service office recorded 5.21 inches of rain for the 48 period. This confirmed several reports of flooded roadways around the island.
News from the talanei reported two boys swept out to sea during high surf conditions due to strong rip currents.
A canoe with 6 rowers capsized in Utulei due to rough seas. Rowers had a difficult time flipping canoe back to its upright position.
Meteorologist Hans reported high surf impacting roadways. Debris from surfs made it difficult for drivers.
MIC Elinor reported downed banana trees in Utulei due to strong winds.

Surfs of 10 to 14 feet were recorded by the PacIOOS aunu'u buoy during the time of this incident. The fisherman who sadly lost his life went out fishing during low tide in the village of Vailoa, which was the normal routine for him. Recent drownings reported were during low tide in combination with high surf conditions.

The national weather service recorded 3.12 inches of rain at the Tafuna Station within the 24 hour period. All residence along flood prone areas were encouraged to evacuate to higher grounds as low lying areas around the island experienced flash flooding conditions. Flooded roadways were also reported by numerous callers and NWS employees making their way over to the office.

Although 1.53 inches of rain was recorded at the weather service office located on the island of Tutuila, satellite imagery showed strong convective clouds and cold cloud top temperatures indicating most of the rain being dumped over Manu'a. One of our trained spotters called to report that the front of her house was flooded and low cars could not go passed her house to get to the other side of the roadway.
Fishermen died due to drowning in Tula (northeastern shore) during low tide conditions. A high surf advisory was also in effect.

The NWS reported wind speeds of 30 MPH with higher gusts that resulted in a power outage noted by the American Samoa Power authority. This even caused conductor clashing, which caused incorrect tensioning of power lines.

Heavy precipitation of 3.35 inches of rain over a 24-hour period was recorded at the NWS Pago Pago. As grounds were already saturated prior to this event, many flooded reports in the typical villages with poor drainage systems like Futiga, Tafuna, and Fagaalu were called in. Also, 2 landslides were observed. 1. in Fagaalu 2. in Fatu ma Futi village.

Impacts from the 16th is combined with the 17th as this weather event was from one day to the next. Heavy crop damage. Several homes lost their roofs.

An official NWS observation. Highest winds recorded was 43G68 mph. Family in Fagatogo Village lost entire roof to their home. Family in Aunu'u lost the roof to their home. Roof blown off museum in Fagatogo. Krispy Crunchy Chicken Restaurant lost the back patio. Radio station KHJ had damage to its communication tower due to strong winds. Power outages in Afono and Vatia. Samoa Airways and Talofa Airways cancelled their afternoon flights due to winds. Crops uprooted in Manu'a.

High surf from an extended period of tropical convection 200 to 300 miles northwest of American Samoa and persistent strong northwest flow, generated an extended period of high surf and water piling onshore along American Samoan's north shoreline.

ASPA reported 25 customers with damages to their house and meters. Power outages scattered across the territory. Flights to American Samoa from Hawaii and Apia suspended.

For a 48-hour period (from the 16th to the 18th) the WSO Pago Pago recorded 5.52 inches of rain. This rain event prompted a landslide in Agugulu that blocked the westbound lane.

Close to midnight on the 17th of January, WSO Pago Pago recorded the highest gust for that day of 46 mph. This wind event caused some damage across Tutuila. On the 17th, the EOC reported a downed tree in Leone that blocked the road and caused traffic. On the 18th, An NWS employee reported downed trees and power lines in Utulei. Another NWS employee reported a tin roof blown off in the village of Nua and Seetaga.

An NWS employee and several callers from the public reported landslides in Amaluia and a minor landslide in Fatu ma Futi. Over a 24-hour period 5.83 inches of rain was recorded at the WSO Pago Pago. This event caused the roads on both lanes to be blocked in Amaluia (there are only two lanes in american samoa), which left residents from villages west of Amaluia stuck westbound until roads were cleared by Public Works later that evening. A minor landslide in Fatu ma Futi blocked only one lane, luckily only a few minor boulders fell and public works was able to clear it up quickly.

Reports of a reef fisherman swept out to sea around 5 PM SST on the 19th. This report was observed on social media and confirmed by the Emergency Operations Center. There were also numerous reports/observations of waves and ocean debris on main roads that impacted south facing shores across the island. Periods of up to 20 seconds were observed by the Aunu'u PacIOOS buoy during this event.

Received a call from EOC Vanu at 1:00 AM reporting flooding in a low-lying area in the village of Amouli. This event caused flooding in a family home, which prompted the family to evacuate to higher ground.

The local weather office recorded 2.21 inches of rain from 10 AM to 2 PM prompting flash flooding in low lying areas and villages with poor drainage systems. Roads in Ottoville, the iliili golf course, and in the front of SAAB Pago were underwater for most of the day. Several reports from the public and the media included an SUV car stalled due to flooded roadways in the front of LDS State Center in Ottoville, and water filled homes in low-lying areas in the village of Malaeimi. After the event, huge crate-sized potholes were uncovered on the fagaima road.

High surf from an extended period of tropical convection 200 to 300 miles northwest of American Samoa and persistent strong northwest flow, generated an extended period of high surf and water piling onshore along American Samoan's north shoreline. Villages along north shores were battered by strong winds and high surf of 20 to 26 feet generating beach erosion, and coastal flooding. Many areas reported debris on roads. Vessels ordered by port admin to anchor outside of harbor due to winds and large surfs.
Total rainfall recorded over a 24 hour period 3.43 inches. Flooding on roads reported in several villages.
Road between Ta'u and Fitiuta cut off by a landslide in Manu'a due to 3.8 inches of rain recorded over a 24 hour period.
Near 50 people in Onenoa were housed in an emergency shelter, result of homes being washed over by waves.

Observations from the PacIOOS buoy reported surfs over 16 feet with steep wave heights near 12 to 15 feet. This combination along with strong winds caused a small craft to capsize near the auasi port of entry. 15 passengers were onboard and had drifted to sea for nearly 2 hours until help was found. Unfortunately 2 passed away during this incident.
Two alia boats battled 24 hours out at sea due to steep wave heights.

Numerous callers driving towards central to eastward villages of Tutuila (Fagatogo to Leloaloa going east) reported all streams over flowing onto the road and into the ocean. This caused flooding and fast flowing water on roadways, rock slides, and numerous cars to be partially submerged in water. The National Parks rain gauge in Pago Pago recorded 3.29 inches of rain during this event.

Saturated grounds from days prior to the 17th enhanced flooding in low-lying areas; rainfall reached 2.25 inches of rain early that morning. This event caused stalled cars across the territory and crater-sized potholes in poor drainage areas.
Several NWS employees reported flooded roadways in villages in the harbor area. Overflowing streams and debris on road from a mudslide in the village of Laulii caused a roadblock across both lanes.

NWS Employee from the village of Amouli and friend of one of the fishermen who lost his life reported the tragic event. Strong rip currents swept two fishermen at the edge of the reef when surfs were transitioning from high to low tide.
Large surfs and strong rip currents swept away an unwary fisherman in the village of Vaitogi.
Vehicle overturns under wet road conditions between the villages of Faganeanea and Matu'u.

After a week long weather event, WSO Pago Pago finally broke its annual rainfall record since 1981, standing near 165 inches of rain. The new record of 189.90 inches took place during this event. Multiple reports from around the Island of clogged drainages, formation of potholes, and business being affected for the Holidays were called in. Reports of flash flooding in low lying areas were mainly reported in the dense populated districts of Tualauta and Tualatai.

Scattered landslides reported around the Island. Motorists driving up the Fagasa Pass shared videos and pics of fallen trees and debris from mudslides blocking the road close to 4 pm. Villagers in Alofau also reported a landslide that blocked the west bound lane. Rainfall from the past 24 hours reported at WSO Pago Pago was 5.13 inches. ||Crews from Public Works and ASPA were at the scene clearing the road while cars in both directions waited.
Estimated winds up to 40 mph caused power outage in Coconut point as reported by a Meteorologist who lived in the area.
The NWS recorded 4.00 inches of rain from August 7th to the 8th. This heavy rainfall event produced flash flooding in low lying areas across the territory.

Rain gauge indicated 2.80 inches of rain over a 24 hour period, which led to three flash flood warnings issued throughout the day. Flash Flooding was reported in areas with poor drainage systems such as the front of cost u less, ottoville, and the golf course.
WSO Pago Pago recorded nearly 2 inches of rain within a 24 hour period, this resulted to the typical flash flooding events near cost u less, ottoville, and the golf course.

The American Samoa Telecommunication Authority confirmed that the landline and internet outage for the Islands of Manu 'a was caused by inclement weather. An underwater fiber cable that connected the Islands of Manu'a to Tutuila broke as a result of high surfs and windy conditions. The efforts to restore communications was difficult as hazardous weather continued on for the next few days.

WSO Pago Pago recording 1.40 inches of rain within a 24 hour period. Though it doesn't seem as much, flash flooding was reported in the harbor area where the Siufaga National Park Site recorded 6.26 inches of rain. Cars were submerged in water in the front of the Pago Pago Catholic church, a low-lying area. A major landslide was also reported in the village of Aua in the front of the Tilo's residence.

During this timeframe, large southerly swells combined with strong winds up to 30 mph caused coastal erosion on the Island of Aunu'u. The seawall was eroded, especially the one near the Assembly of God church.

Talanei newspaper reported extremely high surfs and rip currents that resulted in the  American Samoa Telecommunications Authority (ASTCA) cable break, which left hundreds of Manu'a residents without phone or internet connection for several weeks.
Strong winds associated with the active trough delayed efforts to restore communication services in Manu'a due to the cable break (see high surf event in Manu'a).

Rough conditions observed at the Aunu'u wave buoy showed seas of 7 to 8 feet and peak periods about 18 seconds. These observations confirms high surfs and possible strong rip currents that caused a drowning in the village of Sogi.

A federal contractor on the Island of Ofu reported a landslide that blocked the west bound lane driving through the ofu pass. Rainfall recorded at the local weather station was 2.73 inches within the 24 hour period.

The radio station, 93 KHJ reported a drowning near the Airport during palolo hunting. Sources say the fisherman was not familiar with the area and was possibly swept out due to strong rip currents and high surfs.
The national weather service office recorded 2.45 inches of rain within this 24 hour period. Numerous reports of flooding on roadways and stalled cars were received during this event.
